newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Allianz reveals plans for Indian insurance.
newsitem.headline: Allianz reveals plans for Indian insurance.

text.p: German insurance giant Allianz AG Holding said on Tuesday it planned a joint venture to enter the Indian health insurance market ahead of expected reforms to the country's insurance laws.
The deal embraces Alpic Finance Ltd and Australia's MMI Insurance Group, Allianz's existing Asia-Pacific partner in which it has a 38 percent holding.
"The step underlines both the Allianz Group's and MMI's further move into the Asia Pacific region," Allianz said in a statement.
Allianz has its Asia headquarters in Singapore and revealed its joint venture plan as it opened a liaison office in Bombay.
Alpic, one of India's largest non-banking financial services groups, announced plans in August 1996 to join with Australia's FAI Insurances Ltd to apply for an insurance licence.
That plan was abandoned earlier this month when FAI said delays in the privatisation of the Indian market had derailed the venture and it would open a representative office instead.
Insurance reform was recommended by the Malhotra Committee in 1993 and has been the subject of fierce debate since a change of government in India in April.
Reform is opposed by leftist political parties, including those in the ruling United Front coalition.
Finance Minister, P. Chidambaram backs reform and has slated health insurance as the first segment of the market to allow private sector participation.

An Insurance Regulatory Authority Bill, which if approved would set the framework for the opening up of the decades-old state monopoloies in life and general insurance business, has been before parliament since December 1996.

Insurance in India is dominated by the state-owned Life Insurance Corporation and the General Insurance Corporation, but more than 22 firms from Britain, Germany, Japan, the United States and Switzerland have queued up to enter the Indian market.
"With less than 1 percent of its GDP spent on insurance, there will be an increasing demand for insurance protection in India," Allianz said.
Allianz's ambitions lie well beyond health insurance and the company said it and its partners "also intend to enter the general and life insurance markets once these are liberalised".
